explanation: Verified: 16. The greedy rule — always join the two least frequent — provably produces an optimal integer-length code, which neither Fano nor Shannon managed with their top-down approaches. Huffman found it as a graduate student who had taken the term paper instead of the final exam, and said later he would never have attempted it had he known they had tried and failed.
